closes: Supplies the first published-theory characterization of the module's detector run-length behavior (ARL0/ARL1).
Independently reproduces the Shewhart geometric ARL table (max rel err 0.215%) and the Montgomery Table 9.4 two-sided CUSUM ARL profile via Siegmund 1985 (max rel err 3.03%, 0..2-sigma).
Validates an independent EWMA Markov-chain ARL solver against the lambda->1 Shewhart limiting case.
Grounds the module's locked <=5%% false-alarm / detection-speed KPI in run-length theory (known-parameter regime).
does_not_close: Does NOT establish real-batch acceptability, product qualification, EHS acceptability, or batch-release authority.

ARL results assume i.i.d. normal in-control data with KNOWN mu,sigma; the module estimates limits from a finite baseline, so real ARL0 is shorter and right-skewed (Quesenberry 1993) -- known-parameter figures are a BEST-CASE bound.
No prospective time-ordered 30-batch pilot is checked in; recall/false-alarm on OWNED synthetic universes is unchanged by this receipt.
Siegmund CUSUM ARL is an approximation (gated only over the module-relevant 0..2-sigma small-shift regime).

ewma_module_design_characterization.interpretation: L=3 is a CONSERVATIVE EWMA design: computed ARL0 ~560 exceeds the canonical lambda=0.2 tuning (L=2.86 -> ARL0=370), i.e. FEWER false alarms at the cost of slightly slower small-shift detection. Reported as a computed characterization (grid-converged), cross-anchored by the lambda->1 limiting case above.

cusum_siegmund_vs_montgomery_table_9_4.large_shift_note: Siegmund approximation degrades for shifts >=3 sigma; Shewhart dominates that regime, so it is reported informationally, not gated.

headline: Independent ARL run-length characterization of the live process-QC detector stack: Shewhart geometric table reproduced to <=0.21%, two-sided CUSUM (k=0.5,h=5) Siegmund ARL matches Montgomery Table 9.4 to <=3.0% over 0..2-sigma, and an independent EWMA Markov-chain solver recovers the lambda->1 Shewhart limit. Known-parameter false-alarm budget (union <=0.20 expected/30 batches) sits inside the module's 5% target; estimated-parameter degradation (Quesenberry 1993) is the explicit Phase-1 gap.

kpi_linkage.caveat_estimated_parameters: The <=5% budget check holds for KNOWN mu,sigma. With limits estimated from a finite baseline (Individuals chart) the true in-control ARL0 is materially shorter and right-skewed (Quesenberry 1993), so real per-window false alarms will EXCEED these known-parameter figures. Closing this is the Phase-1 gap.
kpi_linkage.module_locked_kpi: prospective 30-batch pilot: seeded-control recall >=90%, false alarms <=5%, zero false releases
kpi_linkage.small_shift_ranking: memory detectors dominate: at 1-sigma CUSUM (~10) ~ EWMA (~11) detect ~4x faster than Shewhart (~44); the three-detector UNION is justified because Shewhart in turn dominates for large (>=3-sigma) jumps.

non_circularity: ARL baselines are closed-form / Markov-chain results from the SPC literature (Shewhart geometric, Siegmund 1985 CUSUM, Brook-Evans/Lucas-Saccucci EWMA), independent of the module's self-authored synthetic universes and of the existing arithmetic-correctness KPI receipt.
purpose: First published-theory second-signal for the module's SPC detector RUN-LENGTH performance (false-alarm ARL0 and detection ARL1), grounding the module's own locked KPI thresholds (<=5% false alarms, >=90% recall) in Average-Run-Length theory.

theory_reference.cusum: Page 1954 Biometrika 41:100-115; Siegmund 1985 (ISBN 978-0-387-96134-7); Montgomery 2020 Ch.9.1 Table 9.4
theory_reference.ewma: Roberts 1959 Technometrics 1:239-250; Brook & Evans 1972 Biometrika 59:539-549; Lucas & Saccucci 1990 Technometrics 32:1-12
theory_reference.shewhart: Shewhart 1931; Montgomery 2020 8th ed. Ch.6; NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 6.3.1
